report:
### Conclusion  
Scientific research generally **supports** the claim that opening a bedroom window or door improves sleep quality, rather than refuting it.

### Summary of Evidence  
In closed bedrooms, human respiration causes carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) to accumulate overnight. Research shows that opening an internal door or an external window increases ventilation, lowers indoor $\text{CO}_2$ concentrations, and improves perceived air freshness, which positively impacts sleep.

Key findings from indoor air quality studies include:
* **Improved Sleep and Next-Day Performance:** A study published in *Indoor Air* demonstrated that higher ventilation rates and lower $\text{CO}_2$ levels significantly improved objectively measured sleep quality (assessed via actigraphy), reduced morning sleepiness, and enhanced next-day cognitive performance.
* **Ventilation Field Studies:** Research conducted through the Eindhoven University of Technology by Mishra et al. tracked young adults sleeping with open versus closed doors/windows. The study concluded that opening windows or doors effectively reduced $\text{CO}_2$ buildup, directly contributing to better sleep quality.
* **Controlled Environmental Studies:** Laboratory chamber experiments consistently show that lower indoor $\text{CO}_2$ levels foster better sleep conditions compared to elevated $\text{CO}_2$ environments.

While external factors like night noise, outdoor air pollution, or extreme weather can limit practicality in some settings, the health literature demonstrates a clear link between bedroom ventilation and improved sleep quality.

### Sources  
* Eindhoven University research overview: https://bizwhiznetwork.com/study-opening-windows-and-doors-improves-sleep-quality/
* *Indoor Air* study on ventilation and sleep: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/ina.12254
* Mishra et al. bedroom ventilation study: https://research.tue.nl/en/publications/windowdoor-opening-mediated-bedroom-ventilation-and-its-impact-on/
* Experimental study on indoor $\text{CO}_2$ concentrations: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32979003/
